      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Strategy.close shuts down the factory-wide FixedQueuePool",
      "body": "ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and passes the same pool to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close is called by Arroyo when a strategy is torn down, including on partition revocation/rebalance, and it calls self.queue_pool.shutdown(). The factory never recreates the pool, so the next create_with_partitions() returns a strategy that submits to shutdown queues with stopped workers. New messages will not be processed, offsets will never complete, and commits will stall. The strategy should not own/shut down a shared pool, or the factory must recreate/reset the pool when a strategy closes."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",
      "line": 185,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Unbounded work queues provide no backpressure",
      "body": "FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() puts work items unconditionally. The processing strategy's poll() only emits metrics, so Arroyo has no signal to slow down or pause consumption. If workers are slower than the input rate, queue depth grows without bound and the process can exhaust memory. The docstring's claim of natural backpressure is not true with unbounded queues."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",
      "line": 234,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Shutdown flag prevents workers from draining queued items",
      "body": "FixedQueuePool.shutdown first sets worker.shutdown = True for every worker and then calls queue.shutdown(immediate=False). OrderedQueueWorker.run checks while not self.shutdown before each get, so a worker that has just finished an item will exit instead of continuing to drain the queue. Queued work items are therefore abandoned during graceful shutdown, even though immediate=False is intended to allow draining. The pool should rely on queue.shutdown/ShutDown to stop workers after the queues are empty, or only set the flag after draining."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",
      "line": 337,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Close stops the commit loop before draining workers",
      "body": "close() sets the shutdown event and joins the commit thread before calling queue_pool.shutdown(). The commit thread therefore exits after one final commit before the worker threads have drained the queues. Any offsets completed while the workers drain during shutdown are not committed. terminate() has the same ordering issue. The final commit should happen after the pool has drained, or the commit loop should remain alive until after pool shutdown."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",
      "line": 74,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "OffsetTracker iterates all_offsets while other threads can add partitions",
      "body": "get_committable_offsets() iterates over list(self.all_offsets.keys()) without a global lock, while add_offset() can create new partition keys concurrently from the submit thread. If a new partition is first seen while this iteration is running, the dictionary can change size during iteration and raise RuntimeError, causing the commit loop to log an error and skip committing for that interval. A global lock around partition registration/key copying is needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",
      "line": 149,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Failed work items are marked complete and committed",
      "body": "OrderedQueueWorker.run completes the offset in finally even when result_processor raises, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit also completes offsets when decoding/grouping/enqueueing fails. This means exceptions are acknowledged and eventually committed rather than retried or sent to a DLQ. For uptime results, transient failures can drop data unless at-most-once processing is explicitly intended."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py",
      "line": 188,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "FilteredPayload is handled by an assertion in the queue path",
      "body": "SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy passes FilteredPayload values to ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload, which asserts that the payload is not FilteredPayload. The assertion is caught by submit() and treated as an unexpected error, logging Error submitting message to queue and completing the offset. Filtered payloads should be handled explicitly by returning None so filtered messages are skipped without error logs."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",
      "line": 132,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Uses Python 3.13-only queue.ShutDown/Queue.shutdown",
      "body": "OrderedQueueWorker.run catches queue.ShutDown and FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls Queue.shutdown(immediate=False). These were added in Python 3.13. On earlier Python versions, Queue.shutdown does not exist, so shutdown errors are swallowed and worker threads can remain blocked in get(); also evaluating except queue.ShutDown while handling another exception can raise AttributeError. If the service is not guaranteed to run on Python 3.13, this breaks graceful shutdown and error handling."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py",
      "line": 1923,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Error-handling test asserts the opposite of the implementation behavior",
      "body": "test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling mocks ResultProcessor.__call__ to raise and asserts that no offsets are committed. The implementation completes offsets in the worker's finally block even when the processor raises, so the contiguous offsets are eligible to be committed by the commit loop. The test therefore asserts behavior the code does not implement and is also timing-dependent on the one-second commit loop. Either the test should expect the commit, or the consumer should not complete/commit failed work."
    }

findings.title: Strategy.close shuts down the factory-wide FixedQueuePool
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and passes the same pool to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close is called by Arroyo when a strategy is torn down, including on partition revocation/rebalance, and it calls self.queue_pool.shutdown(). The factory never recreates the pool, so the next create_with_partitions() returns a strategy that submits to shutdown queues with stopped workers. New messages will not be processed, offsets will never complete, and commits will stall. The strategy should not own/shut down a shared pool, or the factory must recreate/reset the pool when a strategy closes.

findings.title: Unbounded work queues provide no backpressure
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() puts work items unconditionally. The processing strategy's poll() only emits metrics, so Arroyo has no signal to slow down or pause consumption. If workers are slower than the input rate, queue depth grows without bound and the process can exhaust memory. The docstring's claim of natural backpressure is not true with unbounded queues.

findings.title: Shutdown flag prevents workers from draining queued items
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown first sets worker.shutdown = True for every worker and then calls queue.shutdown(immediate=False). OrderedQueueWorker.run checks while not self.shutdown before each get, so a worker that has just finished an item will exit instead of continuing to drain the queue. Queued work items are therefore abandoned during graceful shutdown, even though immediate=False is intended to allow draining. The pool should rely on queue.shutdown/ShutDown to stop workers after the queues are empty, or only set the flag after draining.

findings.title: Close stops the commit loop before draining workers
findings.body: close() sets the shutdown event and joins the commit thread before calling queue_pool.shutdown(). The commit thread therefore exits after one final commit before the worker threads have drained the queues. Any offsets completed while the workers drain during shutdown are not committed. terminate() has the same ordering issue. The final commit should happen after the pool has drained, or the commit loop should remain alive until after pool shutdown.

findings.title: OffsetTracker iterates all_offsets while other threads can add partitions
findings.body: get_committable_offsets() iterates over list(self.all_offsets.keys()) without a global lock, while add_offset() can create new partition keys concurrently from the submit thread. If a new partition is first seen while this iteration is running, the dictionary can change size during iteration and raise RuntimeError, causing the commit loop to log an error and skip committing for that interval. A global lock around partition registration/key copying is needed.

findings.title: Failed work items are marked complete and committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run completes the offset in finally even when result_processor raises, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit also completes offsets when decoding/grouping/enqueueing fails. This means exceptions are acknowledged and eventually committed rather than retried or sent to a DLQ. For uptime results, transient failures can drop data unless at-most-once processing is explicitly intended.

findings.title: FilteredPayload is handled by an assertion in the queue path
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy passes FilteredPayload values to ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload, which asserts that the payload is not FilteredPayload. The assertion is caught by submit() and treated as an unexpected error, logging Error submitting message to queue and completing the offset. Filtered payloads should be handled explicitly by returning None so filtered messages are skipped without error logs.

findings.title: Uses Python 3.13-only queue.ShutDown/Queue.shutdown
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches queue.ShutDown and FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls Queue.shutdown(immediate=False). These were added in Python 3.13. On earlier Python versions, Queue.shutdown does not exist, so shutdown errors are swallowed and worker threads can remain blocked in get(); also evaluating except queue.ShutDown while handling another exception can raise AttributeError. If the service is not guaranteed to run on Python 3.13, this breaks graceful shutdown and error handling.

findings.title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of the implementation behavior
findings.body: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling mocks ResultProcessor.__call__ to raise and asserts that no offsets are committed. The implementation completes offsets in the worker's finally block even when the processor raises, so the contiguous offsets are eligible to be committed by the commit loop. The test therefore asserts behavior the code does not implement and is also timing-dependent on the one-second commit loop. Either the test should expect the commit, or the consumer should not complete/commit failed work.
